{
 "summary": "Findings: 1 P2, 3 P3. The plan's structure is otherwise sound and every claim it makes about the code checks out. Read-only review; nothing was run.

Claims verified against the code:
- parseConfig is the environment boundary and names the variable on a bad value (src/config.ts:7-12).
- DATA_DIR is always required, so the `<DATA_DIR>/audit.jsonl` default is always computable (src/config.ts:11).
- startServer parses config once and builds an AdminContext per request (src/server.ts:7, 11).
- AdminContext carries actorId and users (src/admin/routes.ts:3-6); nowIso exists (src/lib/clock.ts:2).
- Both success paths are single 204 returns after the directory call (src/admin/routes.ts:11, 20), so "audit only after success" has one clear insertion point each.
- The AuditSink interface with two implementations and a factory is justified: the README names two real deployments (README.md:5-6). Not a premature abstraction.
- recordAudit as the single owner of the best-effort rule is sound.

Findings:

1. Title: Awaiting recordAudit makes the response depend on the audit write
Severity: P2
Location: phase-2/t1
Failure: The plan says each route "awaits recordAudit(...) and then returns its usual 204". The constraint says "an action's response never depends on the audit write". recordAudit only converts a rejection; with the await sitting between the successful users.remove / users.setRole and the 204 (src/admin/routes.ts:10-11, 19-20), the response waits for appendFile. A slow write delays every admin response. UNVERIFIED runtime claim: an appendFile that never settles (stalled or network-mounted DATA_DIR on-premises) would hold the 204 forever although the action already succeeded. The planned test "a sink whose write rejects still gives the 204" covers rejection only, not a pending write.
Fix: Do not await in the routes. Call `void recordAudit(context.audit, event)` and return 204; this is safe because recordAudit never rejects by contract. Keep sink.write invoked synchronously inside recordAudit so the array-sink tests still see the event. Add a scenario: a sink whose write never resolves still gives 204. If the operators actually want the event flushed before the response, that contradicts the stated constraint and needs a decision from them.

2. Title: New environment variables are not documented, and README.md is not in any phase's files
Severity: P3
Location: phase-1/t1
Failure: README.md:8 says configuration comes from environment variables only, and README.md:6 describes the on-premises package only by DATA_DIR. The plan makes stdout the default, so an on-premises install gets audit.jsonl only if it sets AUDIT_SINK=file. Success criterion 2 ("on-premises deployments get audit.jsonl") therefore rests on an undocumented setting. The plan lists README.md under project_docs but never modifies it.
Fix: Add README.md to phase-1/t1's files and document AUDIT_SINK (stdout default, file) and AUDIT_FILE (default `<DATA_DIR>/audit.jsonl`), stating that the on-premises package sets AUDIT_SINK=file.

3. Title: Empty AUDIT_FILE and AUDIT_SINK are left undefined, against the config pattern
Severity: P3
Location: phase-1/t1
Failure: The plan defines the path as "AUDIT_FILE, or `<DATA_DIR>/audit.jsonl` when AUDIT_FILE is unset". The existing boundary treats an empty string like unset (src/config.ts:11: `dataDir === undefined || dataDir === ""`). As written, AUDIT_FILE="" yields path "" and every append fails at runtime, reported only on stderr, instead of stopping startup with the variable's name (src/config.ts:6). AUDIT_SINK="" is likewise unspecified. No test scenario covers an explicitly set AUDIT_FILE either.
Fix: State that an empty AUDIT_FILE is treated like unset, matching DATA_DIR, and say which way AUDIT_SINK="" goes (default or throw). Add a scenario: AUDIT_SINK=file with AUDIT_FILE=/x/a.jsonl gives that path.

4. Title: The stdout sink has no behavioral test; the createAuditSink scenario is not assertable as written
Severity: P3
Location: phase-1/t2
Failure: The scenario "createAuditSink returns the file sink for kind file and the stdout sink for kind stdout" can only be asserted by implementation identity, since the plan exports no distinguishable types. The stdout implementation's output (one JSON line on process.stdout) is asserted nowhere, yet directive d2's completion check claims tests "cover both kinds", and stdout is the hosted deployment's whole delivery path (README.md:5).
Fix: Replace the scenario with behavior through the factory: createAuditSink({kind:"file",path}) then write gives one parseable line in the temp file; createAuditSink({kind:"stdout"}) then write gives one parseable JSON line on a spied process.stdout.write. This subsumes the separate file-sink scenario.

Note, not a finding: the existing context literals `{ actorId: "a1", users }` (tests/routes.test.ts:7, 12) will lack the new required `audit` field. They still pass under bun test because the 404/400 paths never touch it and the project has no typecheck gate (package.json:5-7), but the implementer should add the sink to them, as the plan's "tests pass an object literal sink" implies.",
 "files_modified": []
}

{
 "summary": "Findings: (plan.md reviewed against all of src/, tests/, migrations/, README.md, package.json; read-only, no tests run)

Verdict: the plan should be reshaped before implementation. Phase 2 (stored tier) and phase-1/t2 (shim) should be deleted; the two requirements (badge, move under src/loyalty/) are deliverable with phase-1/t1 plus a reduced phase 3.

1. Title: Stored tier column duplicates a value derived from points_balance
Severity: P1
Location: phase-2 (t1, t2, t3), and summary "The tier becomes a field of the customer record"
Failure: Parallel State. Tier is a pure function of the balance: src/tiers.ts:10-15 tierFor(points), and checkout already derives it at src/checkout.ts:18 `discountFor(tierFor(customer.pointsBalance))`. renderReceipt already receives the Customer with pointsBalance (src/receipt.ts:8,15), so the badge needs no new stored field. The plan gives the tier a second home (customers.tier column, CustomerRow.tier, Customer.tier) kept in step by hand in awardPoints/redeemPoints (Manual Sync, src/customers.ts:25-38), and a third home for the thresholds: the literals 5000/1000 in the migration CASE duplicate TIERS at src/tiers.ts:1-5. Consequences: (a) it contradicts the plan's own constraint "Tier thresholds and discounts do not change" in spirit, since any future threshold change now needs a data migration and SQL edit; (b) success criterion "Checkout discounts are unchanged for every balance" becomes dependent on sync rather than true by construction, since phase-2/t3 switches checkout to `discountFor(customer.tier)`; (c) the production Database adapter is not in this repository (src/db.ts:8 only describes it: "maps each CustomerRow field to the column of the same name"; src/db.ts:9-12 is an interface only), so the plan has no task or proof path for the adapter reading/writing the new column; (d) UNVERIFIED runtime claim: "the stored tier follows every balance change" holds only if every writer runs the new code. The README (line 9) says the pipeline applies migrations in file-name order; if the migration runs before the new code is live, old code writing points_balance after the backfill leaves tier stale. Not traced, deploy ordering is not in the repo.
Fix: Delete phase 2 entirely (no migration, no CustomerRow/Customer change, no change to awardPoints/redeemPoints, no tests/customers.test.ts, leave src/checkout.ts:18 as is apart from the import path). In phase 3, render the badge from `tierFor(customer.pointsBalance)` in src/receipt.ts. Drop the summary sentence about the tier becoming a customer field.

2. Title: Re-export shim at src/tiers.ts has no consumer
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t2
Failure: Dead Code Is Debt (speculative compatibility path). The only importers of ./tiers are src/checkout.ts:3 and tests/tiers.test.ts:2 (repo-wide grep), and phase-1/t1 updates both. README.md:3 and the plan's own constraint state nothing outside the repository imports its modules. So after t1 nothing imports src/tiers.ts; the shim, its deprecation comment, its test scenario (which tests only the re-export), and the unowned "remove in a later cleanup" have no purpose. It also leaves tier rules reachable from two paths, weakening directive d2 "The tier rules live in src/loyalty/tiers.ts".
Fix: Delete t2. Make t1 a real move: delete src/tiers.ts in the same task (it is already in phase-1 files).

3. Title: README still names src/tiers.ts as the owner of the tiers
Severity: P3
Location: phase-1/t1 (files list)
Failure: README.md:6 says "`src/tiers.ts` owns the loyalty tiers"; the plan lists README.md as a project doc but no task updates it, so the doc goes stale after the move.
Fix: Add README.md to phase-1/t1 and update line 6 to src/loyalty/tiers.ts.

4. Title: tierLabel adds a second per-tier table beside TIERS
Severity: P3
Location: phase-3/t1
Failure: Single Source of Truth. Per-tier data already lives in one table, TIERS (src/tiers.ts:1-5: name, minPoints, discount), and discountFor reads it (src/tiers.ts:17-19). A tierLabel returning three hard-coded strings is a parallel list of tiers that must be extended separately when a tier is added.
Fix: Add a `label` field to each TIERS entry ("Gold member", ...) and have tierLabel look it up the way discountFor does; or, if phase 2 is deleted, a single `tierLabel`/lookup used by the receipt on `tierFor(customer.pointsBalance)`.

5. Title: Phase 2 test scenarios lack a runnable proof path
Severity: P2 (moot if finding 1 is accepted)
Location: phase-2/t1, phase-2/t3, phase-2 verification
Failure: (a) t1's scenario "After the migration a row with 1200 points has tier silver" cannot run: the repo has no SQL engine, migration runner or dependency (package.json:1-7 has only `bun test`; src/db.ts is an interface), and no test file is listed for it. (b) t3's scenario "A gold customer gets a 10% discount" has no test file: no checkout test exists (tests/ holds only tiers.test.ts and receipt.test.ts) and none is in the phase's files; the phase verification `bun test tests/customers.test.ts tests/tiers.test.ts` would not run one. (c) Adding required `tier` to Customer invalidates the literal at tests/receipt.test.ts:7, which phase 2 does not list; nothing typechecks (no tsconfig or typecheck script), so the phase verification would not notice.
Fix: Removed by deleting phase 2. If phase 2 is kept, name a checkout test file and a migration proof, and include tests/receipt.test.ts in phase 2.

6. Title: Plan refers to a variable that does not exist
Severity: P3 (moot if finding 1 is accepted)
Location: phase-2/t2
Failure: The task says set `tier: tierFor(nextBalance)`; there is no `nextBalance` in awardPoints/redeemPoints, the balance is computed inline in the `next` object literal (src/customers.ts:27, 35).
Fix: Removed by deleting phase 2.

Plan claims verified as accurate: src/tiers.ts contents (TIERS, Tier, tierFor, discountFor) at src/tiers.ts:1-19; fromRow/toRow one-to-one mapping at src/customers.ts:10-16; awardPoints/redeemPoints as the only balance writers in this repo, src/customers.ts:24-38 (cannot be verified for the out-of-repo adapter or direct SQL); priceOrder applies the tier discount, src/checkout.ts:16-20; customer name line at src/receipt.ts:11, so "directly under the customer name" is well defined; migration backfill thresholds 5000/1000 match TIERS; tests import by relative path (tests/tiers.test.ts:2, tests/receipt.test.ts:2); README statements at README.md:3 and :9.

Resulting smallest complete plan shape: phase 1 = move src/tiers.ts to src/loyalty/tiers.ts, delete the old file, update src/checkout.ts:3, tests/tiers.test.ts:2, README.md:6; phase 2 = add the tier label to the tier rules and the line `Tier: ...` after src/receipt.ts:11 derived from customer.pointsBalance, extending tests/receipt.test.ts (its existing fixture with 1200 points already yields silver); verification `bun test`.",
 "files_modified": []
}

{
 "summary": "Findings: 5 defects in plan.md (1 P1, 2 P2, 2 P3). The plan's claims about the current code all check out; the defects are in sequencing, the retirement of the old-file reader, and verification. Read-only review; probes ran on Bun 1.4.4 in a scratch directory.

---
Title: The old-file reader has a removal date that nothing makes safe
Severity: P1
Location: phase-1/t2 (also context.constraints[2], success_criteria[2], directive d1)
Failure: t2 marks the `currencySymbol` branch `Remove after 2027-06-30`, but the plan never converts old files. The only conversion is "the next save from the settings page writes the new shape".
- src/settings/page.ts:14-16 is the only caller of saveSettings (src/settings/load.ts:40-42); loadSettings (load.ts:26-38) never writes.
- A shop that never reopens the settings page therefore keeps `currencySymbol` on disk indefinitely.
- When the branch is deleted, that file falls to "any other value takes USD with a warning", so a € or £ shop silently becomes USD.
- This contradicts README.md:3 ("every release reads the file that earlier releases wrote") and the plan's own constraint "Installing the new release must keep each shop's currency without a visit to the settings page".
- The date and the "before 3.0" version in the comment have no source in the repo: package.json:1-8 has no version field.
Fix: Drop the removal date and the version from the comment and state the reader as a permanent part of the settings.json contract per README.md:3. This is the smallest shape: no new writer, no new failure branch. If the owner wants the branch to be retirable, that is a design decision to return to them: it needs a load-time rewrite of the file (a second writer of settings.json) plus a removal condition tied to a release, not a calendar date.

---
Title: Phase 1 leaves cart, invoice and receipt broken, and its verification cannot see it
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1 (t1, verification) and phase-2/t2
Failure: phase-1/t1 removes `ShopSettings.currencySymbol`, but its three readers are only changed in phase-2/t2.
- Readers: src/cart/summary.ts:12-13, src/invoices/render.ts:11, src/emails/receipt.ts:6.
- After phase 1 the cart prints "undefined12.50", the invoice prints "12.50 undefined", and receiptEmail throws. Probe: Intl.NumberFormat with an undefined currency throws `TypeError: currency must be a string`.
- tests/receipt.test.ts:5 still passes `currencySymbol: "£"` and would fail after phase 1.
- Phase-1 verification is `bun test tests/settings.test.ts` only, and the project has no tsconfig or typecheck script (package.json:5-7), so the phase is reported green on a broken tree.
Fix: Make the field rename atomic with its consumers. Either merge the two phases into one, or put formatMoney and the consumer switch (phase-2 t1 and t2) in the same phase as the ShopSettings change. In both cases the phase verification is `bun test`, not the single file.

---
Title: The qualitative verification is not runnable and no automated test covers upgrade to display
Severity: P2
Location: phase-2/qualitative_verification; phase-2/t2 test_scenarios
Failure: "Start the app with a settings.json from the current release and confirm the cart shows the shop's currency" has nothing to start.
- The repo has no entrypoint or UI: the sources are six modules under src/, and package.json:5-7 has only a `test` script.
- The constraint "keeps its currency without a visit to the settings page" is otherwise proven only at the loadSettings boundary (phase-1/t2 scenarios), never through to what a screen shows.
Fix: Replace the manual step with one test scenario in phase-2/t2: write an old-shape file (`{ locale: "en-GB", currencySymbol: "£" }`), call loadSettings, pass the result to cartSummary, renderInvoice and receiptEmail, and expect "£12.50" in each. That also covers the existing "same text on all three" scenario.

---
Title: t1 omits the form type that carries the currency
Severity: P3
Location: phase-1/t1
Failure: t1 says "submitSettings writes `currency`" and "currencyOptions returns CURRENCY_CHOICES" but does not name the other `CurrencySymbol` uses that deleting the type from choices.ts breaks.
- `SettingsForm.currencySymbol: CurrencySymbol` at src/settings/page.ts:7 is the public input of submitSettings.
- The return type `readonly CurrencySymbol[]` at page.ts:10.
- `isSymbol` and the warning text built from SYMBOL_CHOICES at src/settings/load.ts:11-13 and load.ts:36.
Fix: Add to t1: SettingsForm gets `currency: Currency`, currencyOptions returns `readonly Currency[]`, and the load.ts guard and warning text are rewritten against CURRENCY_CHOICES.

---
Title: Upgrade changes what Canadian and Australian shops see, and the plan does not disclose or test it
Severity: P3
Location: phase-1/t2 with phase-2/t2 (context.constraints[1])
Failure: The shops that asked for this feature store "$" today with their own locale, and the plan maps "$" to USD.
- Today the cart shows a bare "$12.50" (src/cart/summary.ts:12-13).
- After upgrade, before anyone opens the settings page, formatMoney gives "US$12.50" for en-CA and "USD 12.50" for en-AU (probe output on Bun 1.4.4).
- The mapping itself is a settled constraint and matches what the receipt email already does (src/emails/receipt.ts:3,6), so this is not a wrong mapping. It is an undisclosed visible change on the cart and invoice for exactly the requesting shops.
Fix: State the consequence in the plan and pin it with one scenario (old file with "$" and en-CA shows "US$12.50" until the shop picks CAD), or return the "$" mapping for non-US locales to the owner as a product decision. Do not decide it silently.

---
Plan claims verified against the code (no defect):
- SYMBOL_CHOICES is `$ € £` (src/settings/choices.ts:2).

{
 "summary": "Findings: (7; the plan should be reshaped before implementation. Read-only review, no tests run; all evidence is from reading the 5 source files and 2 test files.)

Smallest complete plan shape that the findings converge on: (a) createApp subscribes the scheduler's existing flush to the store's existing subscribe; (b) the scheduler exposes a derived next-delivery read; (c) SettingsForm reads it. No Preferences field, no attachScheduler, no reschedule, no flag, no isQuiet change.

---
Title: Store and scheduler are made to depend on each other, although the store already has a change-notification surface
Severity: P1
Location: phase-1/t1 (with phase-1/t2 "The scheduler receives the store through a new constructor parameter")
Failure: Bidirectional Coupling. t1 makes PreferencesStore import and call NotificationScheduler (attachScheduler, `this.#scheduler?.reschedule`), and t2 makes NotificationScheduler hold the store and call store.update.
- Today the dependency runs one way: src/notify/scheduler.ts:1 imports only the Preferences type, src/notify/scheduler.ts:28 takes a `getPreferences` thunk, and src/preferences/store.ts:1 imports nothing from notify.
- The store already publishes changes: src/preferences/store.ts:21 notifies listeners after persist, and src/preferences/store.ts:24-27 is `subscribe`. It has no consumer anywhere in src, and the plan ignores it.
- flush already re-reads preferences on every call (src/notify/scheduler.ts:41-43), so "re-evaluate held notifications" is exactly `flush(now)`; `reschedule` adds no sending capability.
- The cycle forces two-step construction (attachScheduler after `new`), which is why the plan needs the optional `#scheduler?.` state.
- The scheduler would hold two routes to the same data: `getPreferences` (src/notify/scheduler.ts:28) and the new store parameter.
Fix: Replace t1 with wiring in createApp (src/app.ts:7-8): `store.subscribe(() => scheduler.flush(now()))`. Drop attachScheduler, reschedule, and the scheduler's store parameter. To keep directive d1 ("before the save completes"), widen PreferencesListener (src/preferences/store.ts:3) to return `void | Promise<void>` and await it at src/preferences/store.ts:21; this is a small contract change that the plan should state explicitly. Move the d1 test to an app-level test, since the store would no longer know the scheduler.

---
Title: nextDeliveryAt is derived runtime state stored inside persisted user preferences
Severity: P1
Location: phase-1/t2 (consumed by phase-2/t2)
Failure: Parallel State. The value is a pure function of three things that already have owners: whether anything is held (`#held`, src/notify/scheduler.ts:26, 46-48), quietHours.end (src/preferences/parse.ts:11), and now. The plan copies it into Preferences and keeps it in sync only at save time, so it is wrong in every other case:
- notify() holding a notification (src/notify/scheduler.ts:32-34) does not call reschedule, so nextDeliveryAt stays undefined. The plan's own phase-2/t2 scenario "fields() returns nextDelivery after a notification is held" cannot pass unless the test also performs a save.
- The minute-timer flush (src/notify/scheduler.ts:40-44), which the constraints keep, sends held notifications without clearing the field. The screen keeps showing a delivery time after delivery.
- store.update persists the whole Preferences (src/preferences/store.ts:20), so the value is written to the saved file. After a restart `#held` is empty (in-memory, src/notify/scheduler.ts:26) but the saved nextDeliveryAt is re-loaded through src/preferences/store.ts:11, so the screen announces a delivery that will not happen.
- Each quiet-hours save becomes two persists and two listener rounds (src/preferences/store.ts:20-21 runs again for the nested update).
- parsePreferences is documented as "the one boundary" where invalid fields take defaults (src/preferences/parse.ts:25-27); "pass it through" adds an unvalidated field there, and no parse test is planned (tests/parse.test.ts is not in the plan's files).
Fix: Do not add the field to Preferences and leave parse.ts untouched. Add one derived read on the scheduler, for example `nextDeliveryAt(now: Date): Date | undefined`, returning undefined when `#held` is empty and otherwise the next occurrence of quietHours.end. The two scheduler scenarios (07:00 next day; undefined after send) remain valid against that method.

---
Title: The #rescheduling flag exists only to break the cycle the plan creates, and it can drop a real save
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t2 ("PreferencesStore sets a private `#rescheduling` flag around the call and skips reschedule while it is set")
Failure: One-Direction Data Flow. update calls reschedule, which calls update; the flag is the patch for that loop, and the third scenario ("The nextDeliveryAt write does not call reschedule a second time") tests the patch, not required behavior.
- UNVERIFIED (reasoned from code, not run): the flag would stay set across `await this.sender.send(...)` (src/notify/scheduler.ts:43). A second SettingsForm.submit (src/ui/settings-form.ts:17-19) that lands during that await would call update with the flag set and skip reschedule, so that quiet-hours change would not take effect at once. That is the plan's headline requirement.
- The defence is also undisclosed: the plan gives no evidence for the reentrancy risk beyond its own design.
Fix: Remove with the two findings above. With no store write from the scheduler there is no reentrancy, no flag, and no third scenario.

---
Title: isQuiet hardening defends a state the parse boundary already prevents, and duplicates the default window
Severity: P2
Location: phase-2/t1
Failure: Speculative Code. No supported producer can hand isQuiet a missing or malformed quietHours.
- Preferences.quietHours is a required field (src/preferences/parse.ts:11).
- parsePreferences replaces any non-HH:MM start or end with the default (src/preferences/parse.ts:19, 35-36), and its doc states "a Preferences value always holds valid quiet hours" (src/preferences/parse.ts:27). tests/parse.test.ts:5-6 already asserts this.
- The store parses on both entry points: construction (src/preferences/store.ts:11) and update (src/preferences/store.ts:19). The scheduler reads only through the store (src/app.ts:8).
- The task would give 22:00 to 07:00 a second home beside DEFAULT_PREFERENCES (src/preferences/parse.ts:16) and the HH:MM rule a second home beside TIME (src/preferences/parse.ts:19).
- The scenario "isQuiet with quietHours undefined" can only be written by casting past the type.
- It is outside the request (take effect at once; show the delivery time) and sits against the plan's own constraint that quiet-hours rules do not change. The plan discloses no evidence for the risk.
Fix: Delete phase-2/t1 and its two scenarios. Rename the phase-2 goal to cover only the settings display.

---
Title: nextDelivery is added to FormFields, which is also the submit input type
Severity: P2
Location: phase-2/t2
Failure: FormFields is the parameter type of SettingsForm.submit (src/ui/settings-form.ts:17), not only the return of fields() (src/ui/settings-form.ts:12). A required `nextDelivery: string | undefined` forces every submit caller to supply a display-only value that submit ignores (src/ui/settings-form.ts:18). The plan does not analyse this call-site impact.
- Reading it from `store.get().nextDeliveryAt` also inherits the staleness in the Parallel State finding.
- The plan stores an ISO time but the screen text is "arrive at HH:MM"; the conversion is not specified. Derived from the scheduler, the display value is simply quietHours.end when something is held.
Fix: Keep FormFields as the editable input. Expose the delivery time as a separate read-only member (a separate method or a separate view type) that asks the scheduler's derived read. That requires SettingsForm to receive the scheduler or a `() => Date | undefined` thunk (src/ui/settings-form.ts:10, src/app.ts:9); add src/app.ts to phase-2 files. Keep the two form scenarios, driven by scheduler.notify instead of a save.

---
Title: The save path reads the wall clock directly, so the d1 test depends on the time of day
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t1 (`reschedule(new Date())`; scenario "Saving quiet hours that ended before now ...")
Failure: Every time-dependent scheduler entry point takes `now` as an argument (src/notify/scheduler.ts:17, 30, 40), and the existing test passes fixed dates (tests/scheduler.test.ts:8, 10). Hard-coding `new Date()` inside update gives the test no way to fix "now", so the directive d1 check must build a quiet window relative to the real clock and can flip around the window edge.
Fix: Give createApp (src/app.ts:6) an injectable clock parameter defaulting to `() => new Date()`, used by the subscribe wiring. The d1 test passes a fixed clock.

Title: Task order and call-site impact inside phase-1 are not workable as written
Severity: P3
Location: phase-1/t1, phase-1/t2
Failure:

- t2 changes the NotificationScheduler constructor but lists neither src/app.ts (call site src/app.ts:8) nor the existing two-argument construction at tests/scheduler.test.ts:7, which has no store at all (`() => DEFAULT_PREFERENCES`).

 "summary": "Findings: 5 defects (3 P2, 2 P3). The core shape (stored per-session expires_at, isExpired reading it, literal 12h backfill) is sound and matches the code; the defects are in persistence ownership, phase boundaries and proof paths.

Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t2 (and context.key_files)
Failure: The plan adds `expires_at` to the table and `expiresAt` to Session, and renames `SessionRepo.deleteCreatedBefore` to `deleteExpired(now)` "(delete where expires_at <= now)". SessionRepo is only an interface (src/auth/sessions.ts:10-15); no implementation exists anywhere in this directory (the tree is only src/auth/{sessions,login,middleware}.ts, src/account/sessions-page.ts, src/jobs/sweep-sessions.ts), and package.json:1-8 has no database dependency. So the code that must write expires_at on insert, read it in byId/forUser, and run the `expires_at <= now` delete is named by no task and no file. If it is not updated, d1 ("every expiry check reads it") is not delivered. The rename also changes an exported interface whose implementers are outside the reviewed tree.
Fix: Name the concrete SessionRepo implementation file and add it to phase-1/t2 (insert/byId/forUser map expires_at; deleteExpired implements the SQL predicate). If it lives in another package, state that and its owner as a dependency of phase 1.

2. Title: Phase 1 changes createSession's signature but its only caller is in phase 2
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t2, phase-2/t1
Failure: t2 makes createSession take `remember: boolean` (position unspecified). The only caller is src/auth/login.ts:15, `createSession(repo, userId, now)`, and login.ts is not in phase 1's files; it is edited only in phase 2. Phase 1 therefore ends with a call site that no longer matches the signature. Its verification (`bun test tests/sessions.test.ts tests/sweep-sessions.test.ts`) cannot see this: neither file imports login.ts, and the project has no typecheck script (package.json:5-7).
Fix: Either put the login.ts call-site update (passing `false`) in phase-1/t2 and its files list, or move the `remember` parameter into phase 2 with the login change. State the parameter position.

3. Title: The migration and sweep test scenarios have no proof path
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t1, phase-1/t2 (test_scenarios), phase-1 verification
Failure: (a) t1's scenario "An existing row created at T has expires_at T + 43200000 after the migration" has no test file (t1 files list only the .sql), no migration runner or DB in the project (package.json:1-8), and phase 1 verification runs only two TS test files. (b) "sweepSessions deletes a remembered session only after its 30 days": after t2, sweepSessions only forwards to `repo.deleteExpired(now)` (today src/jobs/sweep-sessions.ts:5 is likewise one call). With no real repo in the tree, the test must use a fake repo that itself implements `expires_at <= now`, so it asserts the mock, not production code. The real predicate lives in SQL that no test reaches, and it must agree with isExpired's `now >= expiresAt` boundary.

I ran the migration SQL by hand in sqlite3: a row created at 1000 got expires_at 43201000, so the SQL itself is correct on SQLite.

Severity: P3
Location: phase-1/t1
Failure: The default exists only to allow adding a NOT NULL column, but it remains afterwards. Title: Version 1 converter is a compatibility path for a cache the code already rebuilds for free
Severity: P1
Location: phase-1/t2 (and phase-1 files: src/search/upgrade-v1.ts, tests/upgrade-v1.test.ts)
Failure: Speculative Code. The index is a derived cache with no data of its own: src/search/index-file.ts:4-8 states "a file of another version ... is replaced with a fresh build; there is nothing in it that the notes do not hold", and src/notes/store.ts:20 says the notes are the only source of truth. loadIndex already handles a version mismatch by rebuilding and rewriting (index-file.ts:12-21), so bumping INDEX_VERSION (t1) alone migrates every user on their first search. The stated benefit ("keep their existing index instead of waiting for a full rebuild") is not supported by the code: the upgrade path needs the same inputs as a rebuild. cli.ts:9 has already read and parsed every note before loadIndex runs (cli.ts:10), and the upgrade must still call fingerprintOf over every note's full body (build.ts:18) and write the file back. What it saves is only the in-memory tokenize loop (build.ts:21-28), once per user: measured 253 ms for 5000 notes of ~5.4 KB each (27 MB of notes). Because the fingerprint covers tags (build.ts:18), upgradeV1's output under a matching fingerprint is by construction identical to buildIndex(notes), so deleting it changes no observable behavior. Cost of keeping it: a second index type (SearchIndexV1), a second branch in loadIndex, two test files, a contradiction with the loadIndex contract comment and with the existing test "an index of another version is rebuilt" (tests/index-file.test.ts:11-18), and a scheduled removal task ("Remove the converter after two releases") with no owner.

Title: No test protects the version bump, the one thing that keeps stale version 1 files from being served
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t1 (test_scenarios), success_criteria, implementation_contract/d1
Failure: The request says the format moves to version 2, but nothing in the test scenarios, success criteria, or the single directive d1 checks it. loadIndex returns a cached file unchecked when version and fingerprint match (index-file.ts:13-17, cast at :17). If INDEX_VERSION stays 1, an existing file with no `tags` table is returned as SearchIndex and the phase-2 lookup `index.tags[...]` dereferences undefined. The existing test only covers version 0 with fingerprint "x" (tests/index-file.test.ts:15), which is rebuilt on fingerprint mismatch regardless of version, so it would not catch this.
Fix: Extend tests/index-file.test.ts (the owner of this behavior) with one scenario: a file `{version: 1, fingerprint: fingerprintOf(notes), words: {...}}` loads as an index whose tags table holds the notes' tags and the file on disk is rewritten with version 2. Title: Query grammar is underspecified where it meets existing tokenization; plain-word results can change
Severity: P2
Location: phase-2/t1; context.constraints[0] ("Plain-word search results do not change")
Failure: Today search tokenizes the whole query and silently drops anything that yields no word (query.ts:5-7, tokenize at build.ts:13-15, which strips `#` and drops 1-char words). The plan replaces this with per-term matching ("A note matches when it matches every term") without saying what a term does when it yields zero or several lookups. Observed current behavior the plan must either preserve or explicitly change: (a) `a tomatoes` returns both notes (the 1-char term is ignored); a literal per-term rule makes it return nothing. (b) `# tomatoes` returns both notes today; under the plan a bare `#` is a lookup of tag "" and returns nothing. (c) `issue #12` returns the note containing "12" today; under the plan it becomes a tag lookup and returns nothing. (c) is inherent to the requested feature, but it is a result change for an existing query that the constraint and the fourth test scenario ("A query without # terms ...") do not acknowledge. (d) A term such as `plant-tomatoes` tokenizes into two words; the plan does not say they are flattened into the AND set. Fix: State the rule in t1: collect lookup sets as (tag set for each `#x` term with non-empty x) plus (word set for each token of tokenize(term) of the other terms); terms that contribute no set are ignored; no sets gives []. Decide and record whether a bare `#` is ignored (matches today) and note (c) as the accepted change. Add test scenarios for (a) and a hyphenated term so the "unchanged" constraint is asserted on cases that the split can break.

 "summary": "Findings: (4 defects; plan is not implementable as written. Read-only review, no project files changed.)

Verified plan claims that hold: deliverWebhook is one signed POST and throws WebhookStatusError for non-2xx (src/webhooks/dispatcher.ts:25-32); the status is a typed field (dispatcher.ts:12-13); fanOut runs endpoints in parallel with one outcome each (src/webhooks/fanout.ts:9-17); x-relay-event-id is derived from event.id on every call, so it is unchanged across retries by construction (dispatcher.ts:29); HTTP callers take an injectable fetcher (dispatcher.ts:25, fanout.ts:9, src/email/sender.ts:15).

---
Title: t1 hand-rolls a retry loop that src/lib/retry.ts already provides
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t1
Failure: Stubborn Duplication / Shallow Wrapper. The plan lists src/lib/retry.ts and src/email/sender.ts as key files but then never uses them. t1's loop (`for attempt < 5`, rethrow when not retryable or on last try, `sleep(500 * 2 ** attempt)`) is a copy of withRetry (src/lib/retry.ts:12-28): same attempts-including-first semantics (retry.ts:2-3, 15), same isRetryable short-circuit (retry.ts:20), same doubling delay (retry.ts:22), same injectable sleep defaulting to Bun.sleep (retry.ts:8, 13), same last-error throw (retry.ts:27). sendMail already shows the project pattern: withRetry plus an isRetryable classifier over a typed status error (src/email/sender.ts:16-23). The copy also drops the 20% jitter that withRetry applies (retry.ts:4, 23), so all endpoints of one outage retry in lockstep, and the planned tests in tests/retrying-delivery.test.ts would re-test loop mechanics already owned by tests/retry.test.ts:4-22.
Fix: Delete the custom loop. Deliver through `withRetry(() => deliverWebhook(endpoint, event, fetcher), { attempts: 5, baseDelayMs: 500, isRetryable: isRetryableWebhookError, sleep })`. With the loop gone, a separate retrying-delivery.ts module holds only the classifier and one call; put both in fanout.ts (or the classifier beside WebhookStatusError in dispatcher.ts) and drop the new file unless a second caller exists. Reduce the t1 tests to the classifier (400 not retried, 429 and 5xx and a fetch rejection retried) and the 5-try wiring. The scenario "sleeps of 500 and 1000 ms" must become a range assertion (500..600, 1000..1200) because of the jitter at retry.ts:23.

---
Title: fanOut has no way to inject sleep, so the existing fanout test times out and the plan's own verification fails
Severity: P1
Location: phase-1/t2 (also phase-1 verification and success_criteria "bun test passes")
Failure: t2 only says "call deliverWithRetry in place of deliverWebhook". fanOut's signature is `(endpoints, event, fetcher)` (src/webhooks/fanout.ts:9) and the plan adds no sleep parameter, so retries inside fanOut use real Bun.sleep. The existing test has an endpoint that always answers 500 (tests/fanout.test.ts:5-7); after the change it makes 5 tries with real sleeps of 500+1000+2000+4000 = 7500 ms (more with jitter). Probed on the installed bun 1.4.4: a test awaiting 7500 ms fails with "this test timed out after 5000ms". The plan lists tests/fanout.test.ts as a file but states no change to this test, so `bun test tests/retrying-delivery.test.ts tests/fanout.test.ts` cannot pass. The new t2 scenario "500 once and then 200" would also burn 500 ms of real time.
Fix: Have t2 state the missing decision explicitly: add an optional trailing `sleep` parameter to fanOut (additive, existing callers unaffected; mirrors the optional fetcher at fanout.ts:9) and forward it to withRetry, and update the existing test at tests/fanout.test.ts:4-8 plus the new scenarios to pass an instant fake sleep. This is a public signature addition, so it should be named in the plan, not left to the implementer.

---
Title: The "slow retrying endpoint does not delay a healthy endpoint" scenario is not observable through fanOut's result, and fanOut's latency change is undisclosed
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t2 (test_scenarios[1]; context.constraints[1]; summary sentence 2)
Failure: fanOut returns `Promise.all(...)` (src/webhooks/fanout.ts:10), which resolves only when every endpoint has finished. The healthy endpoint's outcome therefore reaches the caller only after the slowest endpoint exhausts its retries. The scenario as written ("does not delay the outcome of a healthy endpoint's delivery") cannot be asserted on the return value and is false for it: the caller now waits up to about 7.5 to 9 s per event where it previously waited one request. What does hold is that the healthy endpoint's POST is not delayed. The plan does not say whether a caller blocking for the full backoff window is acceptable; that is a product decision it leaves open (open_questions is empty).
Fix: Reword the scenario to what the code can prove: with an injected sleep that is held unresolved for the retrying endpoint, the healthy endpoint's fetch has already been called (and completed) before that sleep is released. Add an open question or explicit statement that fanOut still resolves only after all endpoints finish, so its duration grows to the longest retry sequence. Do not change Promise.all to a streaming shape unless the requester asks; that is outside the plan.

---
Title: isRetryableWebhookError retries more than the directive allows
Severity: P3
Location: phase-1/t1 and implementation_contract/d1

No test scenario covers a 3xx or a network rejection, so d1's completion check "covers each class" is unmet for network failures: the five t1 scenarios only exercise 503, 400, 429 and 500.

Fix: Follow the settled constraint: drop `role` from AuditEvent and change the phase-2 scenario to assert actor and target only. If the operators do want the new role recorded, that is a design decision to amend constraint 0 first; then model it as a discriminated union (`{ action: "user.removed" } | { action: "user.role_changed"; role: Role }`), not `role?`.

Severity: P2

{
 "summary": "Findings: (5 defects; the core structural choice is sound)

Sound, checked against code: storing a per-session `expires_at` is the right shape for the security constraint. A stored `remember` flag or TTL class would re-derive expiry from the constants and violate it. Every key_files claim matches the code. `SESSION_TTL_MS` is used only at src/auth/sessions.ts:1,18, src/jobs/sweep-sessions.ts:1,5 and tests/sessions.test.ts:2,6-7, all in phase-1 files. `isExpired` callers (src/auth/middleware.ts:12, src/account/sessions-page.ts:12) need no change, and sessions-page.ts:13 keeps `createdAt`. Arithmetic is right: 43200000 ms = 12 h, Max-Age 2592000 s = 30 d. The new boundaries agree (`now >= expiresAt` and `expires_at <= now`). The backfill uses a literal, not the constant, which is correct. Nothing was run; this is a read-only review.

1. Title: The SQL that stores and deletes by `expires_at` has no owner in the plan
Severity: P1
Location: phase-1/t2
Failure: The plan renames `SessionRepo.deleteCreatedBefore` to `deleteExpired(now)` "(delete where expires_at <= now)" and adds `Session.expiresAt`, but `SessionRepo` is only an interface (src/auth/sessions.ts:10-15). No implementation exists in this tree (it holds only migrations/, src/auth, src/jobs, src/account, tests/sessions.test.ts), and phase-1 `files` names none. The INSERT that must write `expires_at`, the SELECT mapping behind `byId`/`forUser`, and the DELETE predicate are therefore unplanned. Directive d1 ("every expiry check reads it") cannot be shown complete. If the real INSERT is not updated, every new row takes `DEFAULT 0` and is expired at once.
Fix: Name the concrete repo implementation file(s) in phase-1/t2 with the three query changes (insert column, row mapping, delete predicate). If it lives outside this repository, state that as an explicit dependency or blocker with its owner.

2. Title: The sweep test and the migration scenario prove nothing as planned
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t2 (test_scenarios 3 and 4), phase-1/t1 (test_scenarios), phase-1 verification
Failure: (a) After t2, `sweepSessions` is a one-line delegate to `repo.deleteExpired(now)` (today src/jobs/sweep-sessions.ts:4-6). "sweepSessions deletes a remembered session only after its 30 days" can only run against a hand-written fake repo, so it asserts the fake's own predicate, not the real DELETE. (b) The t1 scenario "An existing row created at T has expires_at T + 43200000 after the migration" has no test file: t1 `files` lists only the .sql, and the phase verification runs only tests/sessions.test.ts and tests/sweep-sessions.test.ts. The repo has no migration runner or DB harness (package.json:5-7 has only `bun test`). (c) "A session's expiry does not change when the lifetime constants change (the test builds a Session with an explicit expiresAt)" cannot vary a constant. It reduces to `isExpired` reading `expiresAt`, which the two lifetime scenarios already cover.
Fix: Run the migration and the real repo's `deleteExpired` against a real database in one test: apply 001, insert a row, apply 002, assert the backfill, then assert the delete boundary. Name that file in phase-1 and its verification. Drop scenario (c), or reduce it to one `isExpired` assertion with an `expiresAt` equal to neither constant. Drop the fake-backed sweep test.

3. Title: `DEFAULT 0` plus a one-shot backfill can expire sessions created during rollout
Severity: P2 (UNVERIFIED runtime-ordering claim)
Location: phase-1/t1
Failure: `ADD COLUMN expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` then a single `UPDATE`. Exact claim: a row inserted by the old code after the migration runs but before the new code serves (old insert shape is `{ id, userId, createdAt }`, src/auth/sessions.ts:22) gets `expires_at = 0`. The new `isExpired` rejects it and `deleteExpired` removes it. That breaks the constraint "Sessions that exist when this ships keep their 12-hour lifetime". Whether the window exists depends on deploy order and the unseen INSERT; neither is in this tree, so I could not trace it. The plan states no ordering. The permanent `DEFAULT 0` also turns any future insert that omits the column into a silently dead session rather than an error.
Fix: State the deploy order in the plan. Either guarantee no old-code writes after the migration, or make the backfill re-runnable (`UPDATE ... WHERE expires_at = 0`) and run it again after cutover. Disclose why `DEFAULT 0` is needed (NOT NULL add-column) and that it fails closed.

4. Title: The summary promises a login-form option but no task delivers a form
Severity: P2
Location: summary; phase-2/t1
Failure: The summary says "Add 'Keep me signed in' to the login form", but phase-2 only changes the JSON handler. This tree has no form or client code; login is `POST /login` with a JSON body (src/auth/login.ts:7-9). The checkbox, and the client sending boolean `true` (the plan rejects "yes"), are unassigned. `open_questions` is empty.
Fix: Add the client task with its file, or state that the form lives elsewhere and this plan delivers only the API contract `{ username, password, remember?: boolean }`. Also update the doc comment at src/auth/login.ts:7 in phase-2/t1.

5. Title: Phase 1 changes the `createSession` signature while its only caller changes in phase 2
Severity: P3
Location: phase-1/t2, phase-2/t1
Failure: t2 makes `createSession` take `remember: boolean` with no stated parameter position. Its sole caller, src/auth/login.ts:15 `createSession(repo, userId, now)`, is not a phase-1 file. Phase 1 therefore ends with a type-invalid call, or, if `remember` is placed before `now`, with `now` passed as `remember`: a truthy number that silently yields 30-day sessions. `bun test` does not typecheck and there is no tsconfig or tsc script (package.json), so the phase-1 gate would not catch it.
Fix: Specify the signature `createSession(repo, userId, now, remember)` and move the one-line login.ts call update into phase-1/t2, passing `false`. Alternatively, introduce the parameter and `REMEMBERED_SESSION_MS` in phase 2, where their first consumer appears. In phase-2, derive Max-Age from the created session (`(session.expiresAt - now) / 1000`), so the cookie and the session share one source.",

Title: Version 1 converter is speculative code for a derived cache
Severity: P1
Location: phase-1/t2
Failure: Speculative Code. The plan adds `src/search/upgrade-v1.ts`, a `SearchIndexV1` type, a second branch in `loadIndex`, and two test files to keep a version 1 cache, then schedules its own deletion ("Remove the converter after two releases").
- The index holds nothing to preserve: src/search/index-file.ts:5-7 states the contract ("a file of another version ... is replaced with a fresh build; there is nothing in it that the notes do not hold"), and src/notes/store.ts:20 says the notes are the only source of truth. t2 contradicts that contract and does not plan to update the comment.
- The stated benefit (avoid "waiting for a full rebuild on their first search") is not supported by the code: every run already reads and parses every note (src/cli.ts:9, src/notes/store.ts:21-24) and hashes all titles, tags and bodies (src/search/build.ts:17-19, called at src/search/index-file.ts:15). The rebuild it saves is one in-memory tokenize pass (src/search/build.ts:21-28), once per user. The upgrade path also still walks all notes for tags and still writes the file.
- The existing version gate already does the migration: bumping `INDEX_VERSION` makes src/search/index-file.ts:14 fail for a version 1 file and fall through to `buildIndex` + write at :19-21.
- `SearchIndexV1` is a second home for the index shape next to `SearchIndex` (src/search/build.ts:5-11).
Fix: Delete t2, `src/search/upgrade-v1.ts` and `tests/upgrade-v1.test.ts` from phase-1 files and from the phase-1 verification command. Keep `loadIndex` unchanged. Replace t2's scenarios with one case in the existing tests/index-file.test.ts (extend the test at :11-18): a version 1 file with a matching fingerprint and no `tags` is rebuilt, the returned index has `tags`, and the file on disk has version 2. That is the regression that matters, because a version 1 file cast to `SearchIndex` (index-file.ts:17) would have `tags` undefined and phase 2 would throw on `index.tags[...]`.

Title: Qualitative verification and success criterion use an unquoted # that the shell strips
Severity: P2
Location: phase-2 (qualitative_verification), success_criteria[0]
Failure: "Run `notes #garden`" passes no argument to the CLI. Probed: `bash -c 'echo args: #garden'`, `bash -ic ...` and `zsh -ic ...` all print nothing after the label, because an unquoted word-initial # starts a comment. src/cli.ts:8 then gets an empty query and src/search/query.ts:6 returns []. Fix: Write the command as `NOTES_DIR=<folder> notes '#garden'` in both places, and state the expected paths. The # syntax itself is settled intent; if the quoting requirement is unwanted for users, that is a product decision for the plan owner, not for the implementer.

Title: Term semantics leave reachable cases undecided, and one breaks the plain-word constraint
Severity: P2
Location: phase-2/t1
Failure: "A note matches when it matches every term" does not define these cases, each reachable from current code:
- A plain term that tokenizes to nothing. Today it is ignored: probed `search(i, "a tomatoes")` returns ["a.md","b.md"] (src/search/build.ts:14 drops words of length 1; src/search/query.ts:5). Read literally, the plan makes such a term match no note, which violates the constraint "Plain-word search results do not change". The plan's fourth test scenario does not cover it.
- A bare `#` term. Today `search(i, "tomatoes #")` returns both notes (probed). Under the plan it looks up `index.tags[""]`, which never exists (src/notes/store.ts:15 filters empty tags), so the query returns [].
- The empty-query guard at src/search/query.ts:6 is on tokenized words; a tag-only query has to pass it, and a query with zero terms must still return [].
- Tags that a whitespace-split `#term` cannot address: parseNote splits only on commas, so `tags: Home Garden, #x` yields ["home garden", "#x"] (probed; src/notes/store.ts:15). `#home garden` becomes tag "home" plus word "garden"; `#x` looks up "x" and misses the tag "#x".
Fix: State in t1: plain terms contribute their tokenize output (zero or more words, exactly as today); a bare `#` contributes nothing; a query with no words and no tags returns []. Add scenarios for `a tomatoes` and `tomatoes #` staying unchanged. Record multi-word tags and tags written with a leading # as an open question or an explicit non-goal; do not let the implementer decide silently.

Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t1
Failure: Stubborn Duplication / reimplementation of an existing project mechanism. t1 specifies a hand loop (`for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 5; attempt++)`, rethrow when not retryable or last try, `sleep(500 * 2 ** attempt)`). src/lib/retry.ts:12-28 already implements exactly this: total-tries count (`attempts`, :3), doubling from `baseDelayMs` (:22), `isRetryable` early throw (:20), injectable `sleep` (:8,:13), throw last error (:27). The plan lists retry.ts and sendMail in key_files but never uses them; src/email/sender.ts:16-23 is the established way an HTTP caller retries here. The copy also silently drops behavior: withRetry adds up to 20% jitter (retry.ts:4,:23), while the plan's loop has fixed delays, so all failing endpoints of one event (run in parallel, fanout.ts:10) retry in lockstep.
Fix: Replace the loop in t1 with `withRetry(() => deliverWebhook(endpoint, event, fetcher), { attempts: 5, baseDelayMs: 500, isRetryable: isRetryableWebhookError, sleep })`. With that, deliverWithRetry is a few lines; put it and the predicate in dispatcher.ts or fanout.ts next to their only consumer rather than a new module unless a second caller exists (none in the repo: deliverWebhook is imported only at fanout.ts:1). Severity: P1

The existing test tests/fanout.test.ts:5-7 uses an endpoint that answers 500 forever; after the change it does 5 tries with sleeps 500+1000+2000+4000 = 7500 ms (more with jitter). Probe: a bun test (bun 1.4.4) that awaits Bun.sleep(7500) fails with "this test timed out after 5000ms". So the plan's own verification command `bun test tests/retrying-delivery.test.ts tests/fanout.test.ts` and success criterion "bun test passes" cannot pass as planned, and the plan lists tests/fanout.test.ts as a file but states no change to the existing test. Title: t2 scenario "slow retrying endpoint does not delay a healthy endpoint's outcome" is not observable through fanOut

No per-endpoint outcome is observable earlier, so the scenario as worded cannot be asserted and, read literally, is false: the healthy outcome is delayed by up to ~7.5 s. What actually holds is that the healthy endpoint's request is not delayed. The plan also does not disclose that fanOut's total latency for any caller grows from one request round to up to 7.5 s+ when an endpoint is down.
Fix: Reword the scenario to an assertable property: with an injected sleep that blocks on a manually resolved promise, the healthy endpoint's fetch has been called (once) while the failing endpoint is still parked in its first backoff; then release the sleep and check outcomes.  "summary": "Findings:

Title: The plan creates a second retry engine instead of extending the existing owner.
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t1 (plan.md:35,41).
Failure: Single Source of Truth. The proposed loop duplicates attempt counting, retry filtering, exponential delay, sleep injection, and terminal-error handling already owned by src/lib/retry.ts:1-27. The existing HTTP caller composes withRetry rather than implementing another loop (src/email/sender.ts:15-23). Reuse is not a drop-in replacement: withRetry adds random jitter (src/lib/retry.ts:22-23), whereas the plan requires exact 500/1000 ms sleeps. A fresh probe observed 525.41/1088.49 ms. The plan names the utility but neither uses it nor addresses this concrete difference.
Fix: Keep webhook-specific classification and delivery composition separate from scheduling. Add the smallest shared retry option needed for exact webhook delays, preserving the existing jitter default and email behavior. Delegate to withRetry and cover the new option in its owning tests.

Title: The existing fan-out test will exceed the default test timeout.
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t2 and phase-1 verification (plan.md:50-61).
Failure: tests/fanout.test.ts:4-7 permanently returns 500 for one endpoint and awaits the complete fanOut result. The proposed substitution adds four real sleeps totaling 7,500 ms (plan.md:35). fanOut awaits every endpoint (src/webhooks/fanout.ts:9-17), and its current signature exposes only fetch injection. The planned sleep injection belongs to deliverWithRetry, with no specified way for this fan-out test to control it. Installed Bun 1.4.4 reports a default per-test timeout of 5,000 ms via bun test --help. Thus preserving this existing regression test without a timer strategy conflicts with the planned verification command.
Fix: Specify controlled timers or an existing-compatible test seam for fan-out retries. Preserve the exhausted-endpoint outcome assertion without waiting through real backoff. Include this existing test explicitly in the task's required updates.

Title: The proof path omits network failures and the required complete test gate.
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t1 and phase-1 verification (plan.md:40-45,61); directive d1 (plan.md:75-76).
Failure: The directive requires tests for each retry class, including network failures, but all listed retry scenarios use HTTP responses. deliverWebhook has distinct fetch-rejection and non-2xx paths (src/webhooks/dispatcher.ts:27-32). Existing retry tests exercise generic operation errors, not webhook delivery (tests/retry.test.ts:4-21), and the existing fan-out test covers only HTTP responses (tests/fanout.test.ts:4-7). Also, the explicit verification command omits tests/retry.test.ts even though success requires bun test to pass (plan.md:68; package.json:5-6).
Fix: Add a rejecting-fetcher scenario followed by success, asserting attempts, backoff, and unchanged event ID. Require the complete bun test gate after the targeted tests, especially if the shared retry utility changes.

Title: The independent-outcome acceptance scenario does not match the fanOut interface.
Severity: P2
Location: phase-1/t2 (plan.md:57).
Failure: The plan says a slow endpoint must not delay the healthy endpoint's outcome, but fanOut exposes only one Promise<DeliveryOutcome[]> and resolves it through Promise.all (src/webhooks/fanout.ts:9-17). It exposes no individual outcome promise or callback. A fresh probe confirmed that the healthy fetch completed while the fanOut promise remained unresolved behind another endpoint. Independent delivery progress is supported; independent publication of outcomes is not. A test asserting only the final outcome array would not prove that retries leave other endpoint deliveries unblocked.
Fix: State the acceptance scenario in terms of independent delivery progress: hold one endpoint in a controlled retry wait, prove the healthy endpoint completes its delivery before releasing that wait, then verify the final array. Preserve the current aggregate return contract. If independent outcome publication is actually required, obtain an explicit API decision before implementation.

Evidence coverage: Read the entire plan and every project source/test file. Confirmed the named files, signed single-attempt POST, typed HTTP status errors, injectable fetchers, unchanged event-ID header construction, parallel endpoint mapping, and one final outcome per endpoint (src/webhooks/dispatcher.ts:12-32; src/webhooks/fanout.ts:9-17; src/email/sender.ts:9-23).
